title: How a Tree Becomes a Pencil

lines.say: How does a tree become a pencil?
Cedar logs are sawn into thin slats, then grooved.
The black core? It isn't lead. It's graphite and clay.
Ground with water, squeezed into strings, baked at eleven hundred degrees Celsius.
lines.caption: 1,100 °C

lines.say: More graphite: softer, darker. More clay: harder, lighter.
Glue, the cores, a second slat on top.
So a pencil is really two halves glued together.
Pressed, then cut: six to nine pencils per sandwich.
lines.caption: 6-9 PENCILS PER SANDWICH

lines.say: A metal ring, an eraser, a stamp.
Now it writes the answer: graphite.
Gummy bear, or toy brick? Comment below.
